questions.prompt: Mendel carried out his famous experiments on which plant?
questions.explanation: Mendel crossed varieties of the garden pea (Pisum sativum) and counted the traits in each generation.

questions.prompt: A pure tall pea plant (TT) is crossed with a pure dwarf plant (tt). What are the F1 plants?
questions.explanation: Every F1 plant is Tt. Tallness is dominant, so all of them look tall.

questions.prompt: When F1 plants (Tt) are self-pollinated, the ratio of tall to dwarf plants in F2 is:
questions.explanation: Tt x Tt gives TT, Tt, Tt, tt: three tall and one dwarf.

questions.prompt: Out of 400 F2 plants from a Tt x Tt cross, about how many are expected to be dwarf?
questions.explanation: One quarter (tt) are dwarf: 400 / 4 = 100.

questions.prompt: Round yellow (RRYY) pea plants are crossed with wrinkled green (rryy) plants, and the F1 plants are self-pollinated. The phenotypic ratio in F2 is:
questions.explanation: A dihybrid cross gives four kinds of offspring in the ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.

questions.prompt: A trait that shows up in the F1 generation when the parents have contrasting traits is called:
questions.explanation: The dominant trait is expressed even when only one copy of the gene is present.

questions.prompt: The genetic makeup of an organism, such as Tt, is called its:
questions.explanation: Genotype is the pair of genes; phenotype is the visible trait.

questions.prompt: A plant with genotype Tt looks tall. Its phenotype is:
questions.explanation: The phenotype is what you can see: tall.

questions.prompt: Which cross gives tall and dwarf offspring in a 1 : 1 ratio?
questions.explanation: Half the offspring get T from the Tt parent (tall Tt), half get t (dwarf tt).

questions.prompt: A trait that is acquired during a person's life, such as a cut tail in rats, is:

expected_answer.value: Not passed on to the next generation

options: Not passed on to the next generation
Passed on as a dominant trait
Passed on as a recessive trait
questions.explanation: Only changes in the DNA of reproductive cells are inherited. Acquired traits are not.

questions.prompt: How many pairs of chromosomes does a normal human cell have?
questions.explanation: Humans have 23 pairs (46 chromosomes): 22 pairs of autosomes and one pair of sex chromosomes.

questions.prompt: Which pair of sex chromosomes does a human female have?
questions.explanation: Females have two X chromosomes, males have one X and one Y.

questions.prompt: The sex of a human child is decided by the chromosome contributed by:
questions.explanation: Every egg carries X. A sperm carries either X (girl) or Y (boy).

questions.prompt: What is the chance that a couple's child is a boy?
questions.explanation: Half the sperms carry Y and half carry X, so each child has an equal chance.

questions.prompt: A sperm carrying a Y chromosome fertilises an egg. The child will be:
questions.explanation: Egg X + sperm Y gives XY, which is male.

questions.prompt: Which part of the human eye controls the amount of light entering it?
questions.explanation: The iris changes the size of the pupil to control the light.

questions.prompt: Where is the image formed in a normal human eye?
questions.explanation: The retina has light-sensitive cells that send signals to the brain along the optic nerve.

questions.prompt: Most of the bending (refraction) of light entering the eye happens at the:
questions.explanation: The cornea does most of the refraction. The lens adjusts it finely.

questions.prompt: The ability of the eye lens to change its focal length to see near and far objects is called:
questions.explanation: Ciliary muscles change the curvature of the lens.

questions.prompt: When we look at a NEAR object, the ciliary muscles:
questions.explanation: A thicker lens has a shorter focal length, needed to focus nearby objects.

questions.prompt: A person who can see nearby objects clearly but not distant ones has:
questions.explanation: In myopia the image forms in front of the retina.

questions.prompt: Myopia is corrected by using a:
questions.explanation: A concave (diverging) lens moves the image back onto the retina.

questions.prompt: Hypermetropia (far-sightedness) is corrected by using a:
questions.explanation: A convex (converging) lens brings the image forward onto the retina.

questions.prompt: The near point of a normal human eye is about:
questions.explanation: The least distance of distinct vision is about 25 cm.

questions.prompt: Cloudiness of the eye lens, common in old age, that can be removed by surgery is called:
questions.explanation: Cataract makes vision blurred and is treated by replacing the lens.

questions.prompt: Splitting of white light into its seven colours by a prism is called:
questions.explanation: Different colours bend by different amounts, so they spread out.

questions.prompt: Which colour bends the LEAST when white light passes through a glass prism?
questions.explanation: Red has the longest wavelength and bends least; violet bends most.

questions.prompt: The sky looks blue mainly because:

expected_answer.value: Air molecules scatter blue light more than red

options: Air molecules scatter blue light more than red
Blue light is made by the Sun alone
Red light is absorbed by clouds
questions.explanation: Shorter wavelengths (blue) are scattered more strongly by the very small particles in air.

questions.prompt: The Sun appears reddish at sunrise and sunset because:

expected_answer.value: Light travels a longer path and most blue light is scattered away

options: Light travels a longer path and most blue light is scattered away
Red light is made at the horizon
questions.explanation: Near the horizon sunlight crosses more air, so only the less scattered red part reaches us.

questions.prompt: A rainbow is formed by:

expected_answer.value: Dispersion, refraction and internal reflection of sunlight in water droplets

options: Dispersion, refraction and internal reflection of sunlight in water droplets
Scattering of sunlight by dust only
questions.explanation: Droplets act like tiny prisms. You must have the Sun behind you.

questions.prompt: In a food chain, green plants are called:
questions.explanation: Producers make their own food by photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: According to the 10 per cent law, how much of the energy at one trophic level passes to the next?
questions.explanation: The rest is lost as heat or used in life processes.

questions.prompt: In the chain grass -> grasshopper -> frog -> snake -> hawk, the hawk is a:
questions.explanation: It sits at the highest level of this chain; the grasshopper is the primary consumer.

questions.prompt: If the grass in a chain holds 10000 J of energy, about how much reaches the third trophic level (grass -> deer -> lion)?
questions.explanation: 10000 -> 1000 J in the deer -> 100 J in the lion.

questions.prompt: Why are food chains usually short, with 3 or 4 steps?

expected_answer.value: Energy is lost at each step, so little is left for higher levels

options: Animals do not like to eat each other
Energy is lost at each step, so little is left for higher levels
questions.explanation: Only about 10 per cent is passed on, so very long chains would run out of energy.

questions.prompt: The ozone layer protects living things from:

expected_answer.value: Harmful ultraviolet rays of the Sun

options: Harmful ultraviolet rays of the Sun
questions.explanation: Ozone absorbs most of the harmful UV radiation.

questions.prompt: Which chemicals used in refrigerators and aerosol sprays damage the ozone layer?
questions.explanation: CFCs release chlorine in the upper atmosphere, which breaks down ozone.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a biodegradable waste?
questions.explanation: Biodegradable wastes are broken down by bacteria and fungi.

questions.prompt: Which of these is non-biodegradable?
questions.explanation: Plastics stay in the environment for a very long time.

questions.prompt: Harmful chemicals such as pesticides build up to the highest level in the bodies of:

expected_answer.value: Top carnivores in the food chain

options: Top carnivores in the food chain
questions.explanation: This is biological magnification: the concentration rises at each higher level.

questions.prompt: In which part of the cell does aerobic respiration release most of its energy?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are called the powerhouses of the cell.

questions.prompt: When muscles work hard and oxygen is short, glucose is broken down to:
questions.explanation: Lactic acid build-up causes cramps.

questions.prompt: The first step of breaking down glucose into pyruvate occurs in the:
questions.explanation: It happens in the cytoplasm in all organisms. What follows depends on whether oxygen is available.

questions.prompt: Which statement about aerobic and anaerobic respiration is correct?

expected_answer.value: Aerobic releases more energy per glucose than anaerobic

options: Aerobic releases more energy per glucose than anaerobic
questions.explanation: Complete breakdown with oxygen releases far more energy.

questions.prompt: Which pair shows the products of anaerobic respiration in yeast?
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments sugar to ethanol and carbon dioxide, which makes dough rise.

questions.prompt: The pathway of a reflex action from receptor to effector is called a:
questions.explanation: Receptor, sensory neuron, spinal cord, motor neuron, effector.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct order for a reflex arc?

expected_answer.value: Receptor, sensory neuron, spinal cord, motor neuron, effector

options: Effector, motor neuron, spinal cord, receptor
Receptor, sensory neuron, spinal cord, motor neuron, effector
questions.explanation: Information goes in through the sensory neuron and out through the motor neuron.

questions.prompt: The gap between two neurons where the impulse passes by a chemical is called a:
questions.explanation: Chemicals cross the synapse to start an impulse in the next neuron.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a reflex action?

expected_answer.value: Pulling the hand away from a hot object

options: Pulling the hand away from a hot object
questions.explanation: Reflexes are quick, automatic responses.

questions.prompt: In many reflexes the response is quick because the signal:

expected_answer.value: Goes through the spinal cord without waiting for the brain

options: Goes through the spinal cord without waiting for the brain
questions.explanation: Taking the shorter spinal-cord pathway saves time.

questions.prompt: Which plant hormone helps cells grow longer and makes shoots bend towards light?
questions.explanation: Auxin collects on the shaded side, making those cells longer.

questions.prompt: Which plant hormone helps fruits ripen?
questions.explanation: Ethylene is a gaseous hormone that speeds up ripening.

questions.prompt: Which hormone promotes cell division, for example in fruits and seeds?
questions.explanation: Cytokinin is found in areas of rapid division.

questions.prompt: Which hormone inhibits growth and causes wilting of leaves?
questions.explanation: Abscisic acid slows growth and helps plants deal with stress.

questions.prompt: Which hormone helps the stem to grow longer?
questions.explanation: Gibberellins help stem growth and seed germination.

questions.prompt: The growth of roots downwards towards gravity is called:
questions.explanation: Roots show positive geotropism.

questions.prompt: A covalent bond is formed by:
questions.explanation: Atoms of non-metals share electrons to complete their outer shells.

questions.prompt: How many electrons are shared in a double bond?
questions.explanation: A double bond has two shared pairs; a triple bond has three.

questions.prompt: Which molecule has a triple bond?
questions.explanation: Each nitrogen needs three more electrons, so they share three pairs.

questions.prompt: Compared with ionic compounds, covalent compounds usually have:
questions.explanation: The forces between covalent molecules are weak.

questions.prompt: In the right-hand thumb rule for a straight wire, the thumb shows the direction of:
questions.explanation: The curled fingers then show the direction of the magnetic field lines.

questions.prompt: The magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying wire are:
options: Straight lines parallel to the wire
Straight lines away from the wire
questions.explanation: Their direction follows the right-hand thumb rule.

questions.prompt: If the current in a straight wire is reversed, the magnetic field:
questions.explanation: Direction of the field depends on the direction of the current.

questions.prompt: As you move away from a straight current-carrying wire, the magnetic field strength:
questions.explanation: Field lines get farther apart as the distance from the wire increases.
